meta.title: 15.000€ Mac Studio! FBI Hăckuit, Criza iPhone 18, Agenți AI #CURIOSITY 345
meta.thread_line: 13 threads · AI price war · AI governance · agents in the cloud · Meta glasses · Mac Studio and RAM · iPhone 18 · AI layoffs · wages and jobs · prosumer batteries · cars · hacks and scams · geopolitics

snapshot: AI models got cheaper this week: Opus 5 (Anthropic) is ~40% more efficient than its predecessor, GPT-6 Luna costs $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens, and Buhnici expects another **10-20x** drop by year-end.

Agents are moving to the cloud: Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok Bot and Instinct already read mail, negotiate with other agents and run on their own cloud computers; hardware (pendants, glasses) is just the microphone.
Meta Connect brought $1,300 display glasses (spring 2027) plus a Muse pendant; Buhnici likes the DisplayPort-over-USB-C spec, not the idea of walking around in them.
Mac Studio with 1.2 TB/s memory bandwidth is the only box for 500 GB local models; RAM makers have two years of orders booked and won't add capacity, so prices stay high.
iPhone 18 wait times jumped to 23 days (Pro) and 30 days (Pro Max) after JPMorgan's 7/19-day readings; Romanian price starts at 7,700 RON.
Romanian IT firms are laying off staff after moving everyone onto Claude Code; Buhnici argues market forces, not villains, drive it, and urges 6 months of savings.
ShinyHunters hacked the FBI site and demand an 8-figure ransom; MultiversX froze its chain after a post-upgrade mint exploit; fake job interviews now steal developers' keys.
At the UN, Amodei, Altman and others pitched AI governance while Xi met Trump in Washington; Buhnici sees Romania missing the conversation entirely.

themes.status: RELEASED THIS WEEK — OPUS 5, GROK 4.7, GPT-6 SOL/LUNA, GEMINI 3.8 FLASH
themes.title: Models get cheaper and sharper at once: Opus 5, GPT-6 Sol/Luna and Grok 4.7 start a price war
themes.lead: For the first time in months a heavy user didn't burn through the usage window, because efficient models now carry frontier-grade work.
bullets: **Opus 5** (Anthropic): at least 40% more efficient than the previous generation, 'works like Fable at half the price', $4 input / $20 output per million tokens; Buhnici moved most of his coding there and kept 10% usage unused.
Fable 5.1 is very good but consumes heavily; Sonnet 5.5 costs only 30% more than Sonnet 5, which he runs for the store and site agents that talk to customers.

**GPT-6 Sol** (OpenAI): $2 input / $10 output, claimed to deliver 90-95% of Astra at one fifth of the cost per task; **GPT-6 Luna**, the Sonnet-5-class tier, is $0.10 / $0.50 — about 30x cheaper than the same capability two months ago.

Grok 4.7 (xAI, released September 21): 2.1 trillion parameters, 40% better than its predecessor, context cut from 1M to 500k tokens, price unchanged at $2 / $6; Buhnici doesn't count it as frontier but it powers Grok Bot.

Google shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash, text-to-speech and a voice-to-voice model, with no Pro newer than 3.1 yet; voice cloning is available everywhere except Europe, and Buhnici chose not to clone voices in his own content.
Cost tip: caching cuts costs ~60%, so start a new task per job in Claude Code instead of piling onto the last window, where every command re-reads the whole prior context.
Race is now price per token between the US labs, the Chinese labs and whoever owns hardware; Buhnici expects costs to fall another 10-20x by year-end while memory gets dearer.

themes.status: UN GENERAL ASSEMBLY WEEK — AI LABS AT THE SECURITY COUNCIL
themes.title: AI labs ask governments for licences while Washington says the product is yours
themes.lead: The labs want state authorization so responsibility moves outward, and the US government is pushing it straight back.
bullets: Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, Marc Benioff and Clem Delangue addressed the UN Security Council on AI policy and international security; Buhnici reads it as a request that foreign ministries own AI responsibility.
Anthropic and Accenture each put in **$1B** to build a body that evaluates AI models; critics call it regulatory capture, a route to state-validated licensing.
Washington's reply, as he tells it: if you worry about speed, slow down — it's your product, you take the money, you answer for what it does.
Governor Gavin Newsom, a possible presidential candidate, wants a red 'kill switch' for AI; California can regulate locally without Washington.
Trump announced an AI task force and wants AI rebranded as superintelligence; the host jokes the announcement came with AI-generated pictures.
Buhnici's read of the labs' motives: each cares about keeping Altman and Musk from getting ahead; he expects the labs to end up testing each other's models.
Romania's foreign ministry runs an AI that monitors the press; he asks whether anyone there can speak on AI policy.
themes.watch: Host reads the motives of named executives; the Accenture body is described only from commentary, and the captions garble its name.

names.name: Accenture (ACN)
names.blurb: Co-funds a $1B-each model-evaluation body with Anthropic.

themes.status: AGENTS MOVE TO THE CLOUD — AUTUMN-WINTER 2026-27
themes.title: Agents get their own cloud computer: Muse, Grok Bot and Instinct contact you first
themes.lead: The mega-trend he follows into winter 2026-27 is agents that run in the cloud, plug into your mail and WhatsApp, and start the conversation themselves.
bullets: **Meta Muse** (model Muse Spark 1.3) launched this month; it reads calendar and mail, can book flights and order food, and sits inside WhatsApp.

xAI's Grok Bot demo: SpaceX engineers launched a company with a team of agents in public; the model runs on Nvidia boards, files live in an Amazon bucket, each agent has its own Chromium-based computer, browser and Gmail connector.

Buhnici has run Grok Bot for 2-3 weeks: it messaged him at 4:45 am with a mail summary, flagged an unpaid invoice and a grid outage near Corbeanca, and negotiated a brand deal with a counterpart AI until a human had to sign.
**Instinct** (a friend gave him access) works over iMessage/WhatsApp with no app; he doesn't let it act yet — 'I don't trust it'.
Brand email is ~90% cold calling; an AI filter between him and others also protects against malicious attachments such as a fake offer .xlsx.

Form factors will vary — phone stays for a long time (screen, camera, sensors); pendants, pins and glasses become the microphone to a cloud agent. Rabbit's hardware failed: unstable, not native, too early.
Apps are being replaced by agents in conversation; his own new site is a vibe-coded mini web app with a social-style feed of everything he posts.

themes.title: Meta Connect: display glasses with DisplayPort, a Muse pendant, and a rival to Vision Pro
themes.lead: Meta raised the bar for headset hardware, but he'd buy it for the DisplayPort link, not for Muse or walking around.
bullets: Glasses weigh about 100 g plus a ~300 g external battery/compute unit; micro-OLED, 'infinite 5K' claim, ~2,4K per eye, 70° field of view, ~37 pixels per degree (60 is the invisible-pixel limit), 12 MP camera.
Snapdragon Reality Elite chip, 12 GB RAM and a local Llama 4 for 'hey Meta' commands; foveated rendering follows the eyes; 120 Hz claimed, battery 3 hours, 45 W charging.
**$1,300**, available spring 2027, 'first VR glasses with DisplayPort over USB-C' — Buhnici plans to buy them for that; expects manufacturing constraints. Meta says it worked 10 years on them.
Positioned against Apple's Vision Pro, which Apple has stopped pushing; Meta calls them far lighter at similar capability; IMAX/Dolby certifications he dismisses as branding.
The Muse pendant listens to WhatsApp chats and notes; Radu's verdict: a tamagotchi that eats your information, not just your time.
EssilorLuxottica and Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses now describe what the wearer sees; Nuance Audio glasses act as a hearing aid (~€1,000 / $899, 10-hour battery, FDA-cleared, iPhone calls only).

themes.status: M5 ULTRA 512 GB OPTION — LATE OCTOBER
themes.title: Mac Studio becomes the local-AI box while RAM stays locked up for two years
themes.lead: With 1.2 TB/s memory bandwidth Apple has the only machine for 500 GB local models, and the RAM supply behind it won't loosen.
bullets: **Mac Studio M5 Max / M5 Ultra**: first time at 1.2 TB/s memory bandwidth; the 512 GB RAM option for M5 Ultra arrives late October, price not announced; Thunderbolt links let you chain machines.
Configured in the video: ~10,800 RON with 1 TB storage, ~11,300-12,000 with 2 TB, 18,299 RON with 16 TB, plus AppleCare and a UPS (spoken figures vary).
Alternative is Nvidia Spark boxes: they run ~$4,000-10,000 each and need a ~$10,000 switch to link, so for 500 GB models he says Apple has no competitor; he claims Mac Studio is built in the US.
Waiting lists exceed iPhone's; people buy Mac Studios, use them six months and resell at a profit; Apple doesn't sell directly in Romania, so iStyle orders take long.
RAM makers have orders booked two years ahead and refuse to expand after earlier busts; DDR5 speed gains stalled, CUDIMM went silent, and high-bandwidth memory is traded 'like a commodity'.
New **Mac mini** (M6 / M5 Pro): soldered storage; 128 GB SSD runs at half the speed of 256, 512 is double 256, and the M6 512 GB model passes 6 GB/s — PCIe 4.0 class, 'more than enough'.
Hardware rule of thumb: 32 GB RAM, take care of it; 128 GB, you're strong; 192 GB and up, you're emperor.
themes.watch: Several hardware figures are read live off Apple's configurator and a Romanian retailer; the 15.000€ in the title is not stated as a price in the discussion.

names.blurb: Mac Studio and Mac mini; unexpected demand for memory-hungry machines, no preferential memory contracts.

themes.status: IPHONE 18 PRO / PRO MAX — SUPPLY SHORT
themes.title: iPhone 18 wait times jump to a month as buyers skip the foldable
themes.lead: Last week's 7-day delivery reading was misleading; Pro Max now takes 30 days and resells at a premium.
bullets: JPMorgan's global averages of 7 days (18 Pro) and 19 days (Pro Max) versus 15 and 24 last year have stretched to **23 and 30 days**; resale premium is 10-20% (8,600 RON phone → ~10,000).

Buhnici's read: people watched the Duo (foldable) launch, balked at the price and bought a 18 Pro instead; Apple didn't expect Duo to be the bestseller — at $500 everyone would buy it. Duo preorders open in about three weeks.
Romanian start price is 7,700 RON for the 256 GB Pro; the Pro Max 2 TB is 16,500-16,700 RON, ~$1,000 above the base Duo; the new phone fits 17 Pro cases.
Reports of scratches on blue units, some even sealed at US Walmart; the guess is aluminium and Indian production.
Advice: skip if you own a 17; consider if your phone is 2-3 years old; for creators he'll show camera tests later.

Phones as multicam: three phones plus an iPad overheat and aren't reliable for long production; he points to a 500 € camera with USB streaming or a Lumix, and small cheap cameras for fixed-location podcasts.

names.name: Apple (AAPL)
names.blurb: iPhone 18 demand pulled into Pro/Pro Max, delivery pushed to 23-30 days.

names.name: JPMorgan (JPM)

themes.status: ROMANIAN IT LAYOFFS — CLAUDE CODE REPLACES HEADCOUNT
themes.title: Romanian IT firms lay off after switching to Claude Code: market forces or bad bosses?
themes.lead: The host argues competition pushes every firm toward efficiency, while the co-host insists revenue and sales come first.
bullets: A Romanian IT manager cut 10 people last month, 5-10 more this week and ~10 yesterday after giving everyone a monthly Claude Code subscription; several laid-off staff offered to work for 'anything above zero'.
Another firm cut tens of percent of a firm of dozens within a month; the laid-off asked for freelance work right away.
Buhnici: firms must reach ≥15% profit to beat inflation; 'the only thing that wins forever is the lower price' — a rival using the same tools forces your hand.
Radu: the first fix should be sales and customer loss, not staff; replacing people with an AI trained by them is shortsighted, and a new hire costs more and takes long to integrate.
Costs of churn: factory turnover 10% overall, ~30% in unskilled roles where +100 RON elsewhere moves people; 'thousands of firms closed this year' and tens of thousands more to come.
Labor is heavily taxed — nearly double the pay for an employer; one of his suppliers raises tariffs 36% from October 1.
Best case: employer and employee ask each other what they want; unsaid things don't exist. He invites comments, 'treat them like Glassdoor, no IPs'.

quote.text: Singura chestie care castiga forever este pretul mai mic.

themes.watch: Layoff anecdotes are second-hand from unnamed Romanian firms; the host says he knows one case first-hand.

themes.title: Romania's wage and jobs data: 5,820 RON net doesn't cover a big-city life
themes.lead: Official unemployment looks low at 3.25%, but more people are without work than a year ago and a large city is out of reach on the average wage.
bullets: INS: average net wage **5,820 RON** in July (+86 RON), gross 9,709 RON; the host says the average is pulled up by big-city costs.
His big-city budget: rent 2,000-2,500 RON, 1,000 for utilities/phone/internet, ~1,500 for food → 3,500 before food; two people can save ~25%.
Many move back in with parents, children included; Toscana example: €1,200 a month versus ~€1,700 needed in Bucharest.

Official unemployment 3.25%, 25,989 registered; 526,800 people jobless aged 15-74, up from a year ago; ~30% of the unemployed have primary or no schooling, a third high school, under 5% university graduates.
Vacancy map: Satu Mare 162 openings, Brasov 573; the host calls the map unserious; the 'gap goes to export' as jobless Romanians leave abroad.
Advice: reskill; he hears fibre-optic splicers, electricians and plumbers are in demand and quotes a plumber at 1,000 RON just to assess a leak.
Rule: keep **six months** of living expenses — over 3/4 of people live paycheck to paycheck.
Romanian president Nicusor Dan told JPMorgan it's 'just political noise'; the host says the country will borrow hundreds of billions over the coming years.
themes.watch: Cost-of-living figures are the host's on-air estimates, not a published survey.

names.name: JPMorgan (JPM)
names.blurb: Where the Romanian president reassured lenders, per the host.

themes.title: Prosumer rules slip while the state-funded battery programme opens to existing owners
themes.lead: The regulator missed its own deadline for the prosumer law norms, and the battery subsidy gets friendlier to people who already have storage.
bullets: ANRE missed the legal 24 September deadline for the prosumer norms and opened another consultation (comments to October 1, then a public debate); the host trusts the prosumer association's amendments.
Utility emails with autumn offers can be 'pernicious': paste any offer or contract into an AI and compare it with the market.
Battery programme: budget **400M RON**, funding up to 75% of project value, max 15,000 RON with VAT, own contribution at least 25%.

Changes: minimum system capacity cut from 12 to 10 kWh, standard cost raised (1,500 RON/kWh with VAT — host thinks 500-1,000 is fair), existing-battery owners now allowed; lithium-ion, LFP and sodium accepted, lead-acid excluded.
He may apply with a larger battery (he has ~40 kWh, wants ~80) to charge his EV overnight from storage.
Cernavoda is in its eighth week offline amid drought; day-ahead price ~1.3 RON/kWh before fees on the Yellow Grid app.
themes.watch: Mixed units were spoken for the battery cost cap; 'per kW' and 'per kWh' used interchangeably in the captions.

themes.status: TOTAL COST OF OWNERSHIP — DACIA SPRING TEST DEBATE
themes.title: Chinese brands take 11% of Romania's car market; TCO shows the real price per km
themes.lead: A Dacia Spring costs about 1 RON per km on total cost, and the host says cheap used cars still win on pure cost.
bullets: Chinese makers hold ~11% of Romanian registrations: **BYD** 4% share (3,465 cars), MG 2,368, Chery 257; in July BYD registered 672 and reached 5th place with 5.7%.
About 60% of BYD sales are plug-in hybrids; the host warns they fit only narrow scenarios; Volkswagen and Porsche are reported to be struggling.
His theory for the rise: Chinese dealers are live on social media every day; a woman paying 4,000 RON a month for petrol switched to an Omoda and is 'much happier'.
TCO calculator on his site: purchase price, resale, insurance, service, tires over lifetime divided by km; he put four electric cars under €18,000 at roughly 1 RON/km.
Counterpoint: a €3,000 used car at 15,000 km a year with ~9 L/100 km spends ~0.9 RON/km on fuel alone and avoids financing and the upfront outlay.

Rovinieta rises from October 1 (roughly 200 to 250 RON); A7 Moldova motorway has 270 km without rest stops, nobody bids for service areas — 'state business is never profitable' and station margins are thin.
themes.watch: Registration figures are read aloud from economica.net and may mix year-to-date with monthly numbers.

names.name: BYD
names.blurb: Fifth-largest brand in Romania in July, mostly plug-in hybrids.

names.name: Dacia
names.blurb: Spring EV test at ~1 RON/km TCO; readers disputed the maths.

themes.status: FBI SITE HACKED — MULTIVERSX CHAIN HALTED
themes.title: FBI hacked, MultiversX halted, fake job interviews steal keys
themes.lead: Three security stories in one week: a hacker group extorting the FBI, a chain freeze after a mint exploit, and deepfake recruiters.
bullets: **ShinyHunters** hacked the FBI's site after a vulnerability disclosure wasn't credited to them; they demand an eight-figure sum or they'll publish data showing which government bodies secretly paid hackers.

MultiversX halted its network after the Supernova upgrade: someone exploited new code and minted tens of millions of EGLD ('Gold' in captions); validators blocked wallets, and some minted coins were already sold.
Rolling the chain back needs validators, Buhnici among them; the whole crypto market was rising that week, and he discussed it on 'Follow the Money' with Andrei Bratucu.
Job-interview scam: a fake recruiter, often AI-rendered, asks you to run code on your own machine and steals keys; the final test is asking them to put a hand in front of their face.
Scammers still use cheap AI and avatars; Scammer Payback is his go-to relaxation channel; a prompt-hijack clip made a scam bot spout nonsense.
Android 17 beta code hints at 'unlock with Google account' for a forgotten PIN; Chrome on Windows now asks to start at boot; Pixel's camera app got a built-in teleprompter.
Romania's land registry agency ANCPI left citizens without cadastre documents for two months after its own attack and rebuilt the database from paper.
themes.watch: ShinyHunters' claims about government payments come from the group itself, relayed through the hosts.

names.name: MultiversX (EGLD)
names.blurb: Chain frozen after a post-upgrade mint exploit; host is a validator.

themes.status: UN WEEK — XI AND TRUMP IN WASHINGTON
themes.title: UN week, AfD isolation and why Russia doesn't crack
themes.lead: Romania argues over its own circus while AI, Iran, Gaza and Ukraine are on the table in New York and Washington.
bullets: Xi Jinping met Donald Trump in Washington during UN General Assembly week; AI, Iran and Ukraine were on the agenda; Romania's president spoke briefly then went to JPMorgan.

Germany plans to restrict AfD access to intelligence after it won a second state vote (38.2% in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt); the host calls it a repeated historic mistake — 'when you treat someone like that a tyrant will rise'.
Germany's OPLAN is the response plan if Russia attacked; the stated fear is AfD donors leaking it to Russia.

Lavrov at the UN: Russia wants a full peace deal rather than a pause on energy-infrastructure strikes; Ukraine's refinery bombing continues; Putin urged soldiers to vote; Prof. Gosu claims a stealth mobilisation of ~300,000 more men is under way.
Host's question: Russia's economy is called disastrous — why doesn't inflation gallop? Probably China.
Dismissal of the Georgescu arrest news as 'another feint to distract'.
themes.watch: Political claims come from conversation; the mobilisation figure is attributed to Prof. Gosu's Substack.

takeaways.title: Route high-volume, non-sensitive tasks to the cheap tier (GPT-6 Luna, Sonnet-class) and keep a frontier model for hard work.
Start a new Claude Code task per job so caching applies instead of re-reading one huge context.
Hold on to machines with 128 GB+ RAM and price a Mac Studio against Nvidia Spark clusters before buying local-AI hardware.
Never run code a recruiter sends; use an AI assistant as a first filter for inbound offers and attachments.
Paste utility offers and contracts into an AI to compare them, and track ANRE's prosumer norms before the battery programme opens.
Keep six months of living costs in reserve and reskill toward trades or AI-adjacent skills.

Robot boxing: Frankie Lapena took a heavy punch from a robot in a ring; the host expects robot leagues but human fights to stay first.
The 'Gen Zer' stare: people swipe left in real life; his advice is to give others a path of empathy because everyone is 'fried' and cooperation is ongoing negotiation.
Podcast tools: Adobe Podcast's cloud noise removal beats its Premiere plugin; the iPhone's built-in noise cancelling was aggressive but worked on an A7 motorway clip.
TV and books: Lioness S2, Slow Horses, Mobland S2, the new Grand Tour, Severance; David Neacsu's 'Cartea inimilor' (Humanitas), after 'Cartea inaltimilor'.
Members' interview with Adrian Luben (Mars Gizmo), recorded at IFA Berlin after the organisers lost the raw footage.
Starship's next flight slipped from September 22 to 28; Cernavoda is in its eighth week offline, so the hosts joke on which restarts first.

glossary.def: Purchase price minus resale plus running costs, divided by kilometres driven, giving the true cost per km.
A household that both consumes and sells electricity, typically via rooftop solar.
A display technique that renders full detail only where the eye looks.
Angular resolution of a headset; about 60 PPD is the limit at which pixels vanish for 20/20 vision.
An AI agent with no app or interface of its own, reached through messaging such as WhatsApp or iMessage.
Reusing an already-processed context so repeat calls cost far less.
